response.reason: The cited clause, Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 Art. 26(3), establishes the requirement that when the country of origin or place of provenance of a food is given and it is not the same as that of its primary ingredient, the origin of the primary ingredient must also be given or indicated as different. The verdict turns on this requirement, stating that both origins are declared and are the same, thus satisfying the clause. The clause is directly relevant and supports the legal grounding of the verdict.
